original_question: Determine whether there are only finitely many hyperkahler manifolds, up to deformation, in each dimension.
target_in_paper: Section 2.5 (Boundedness), Conjecture 1: "There are finitely many hyperkähler manifolds (up to deformation) in each dimension."
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's target almost verbatim: it asks about finiteness of hyperkähler manifolds up to deformation in fixed dimension, which is exactly the content of Conjecture 1 in the boundedness section.
missing_details: The paper is discussing compact hyperkähler manifolds; this compactness is implicit from the section title and the basic definition used earlier.

To make the question stand alone, 'hyperkähler manifold' should be understood in Beauville's sense used in the paper: a compact simply-connected Kähler manifold carrying an everywhere nondegenerate holomorphic 2-form, equivalently with H^0(X, Ω_X^*) = C[σ].
The relevant dimension is complex dimension, and in this setting it is necessarily even; so one may state it as dimension 2r for each integer r >= 1.
The phrase 'up to deformation' means up to deformation equivalence, i.e. finiteness of deformation types rather than finiteness of isomorphism classes.

No extra assumptions such as projective, polarized, fixed Beauville-Bogomolov form, fixed Fujiki constant, or bounded Betti numbers are part of the conjecture itself; those only appear nearby as partial evidence or related boundedness results.
refined_question: For each integer r >= 1, are there only finitely many deformation types of compact hyperkähler manifolds X of complex dimension 2r, where hyperkähler is understood in Beauville's sense: X is a compact simply-connected Kähler manifold with an everywhere nondegenerate holomorphic 2-form σ and H^0(X, Ω_X^*) = C[σ]?
justification: The draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation: Section 2.5 states exactly the boundedness conjecture as Conjecture 1. The only additions needed are the paper's ambient notion of hyperkähler manifold and the meaning of dimension and deformation. Earlier in Section 2.1, Beauville identifies the class of manifolds he calls hyperkähler (also called irreducible holomorphic symplectic), so adding compactness, simple connectedness, the Kähler condition, and the holomorphic symplectic form makes the question self-contained and faithful to the paper. The surrounding discussion in Section 2.5 confirms that the conjecture is genuinely about finiteness of deformation types in each fixed dimension, while the unnumbered Huybrechts remark and Proposition 2 on fourfolds are only partial finiteness evidence and should not be folded into the main question.
